SNACS review rules (v2.6; from authorized examples)

Represent each target as [scene_role, lexical_function]; both labels use p. prefixes. Role is the relation in context; function is the lexical contribution of the adposition or marker. They can match or differ through construal. Choose from complement plus governing predicate/construction, not the preposition alone.

Quantity and partitive of:
- ‘Each of you’ / ‘one of them’: p.QuantityItem/p.Whole, where a quantifying expression denotes a subset/member relative to a set.
- ‘plenty of options’ and ‘lots of restaurants’: p.QuantityItem/p.QuantityItem (measure/amount construction; complement is the quantity-bearing item, not a whole set).
- Material/content after batch (‘batch of wings’): p.QuantityItem/p.Stuff. Kind/type ‘kind of space’: p.Species/p.Species.

Emotion, evaluation, and possession:
- ‘proud/pleased with contributions/that one’: p.Stimulus/p.Topic; the complement evokes the emotion and is its topic. ‘problem with the tile’ is p.Topic/p.Topic.
- Possessive linked to an event noun where possessor is the actor (‘your contributions’, ‘her help’): p.Agent/p.Gestalt.
- Body part possessed by its whole (‘my hair’): p.Whole/p.Gestalt.
- Ordinary ownership (‘your money’, ‘my dogs’, ‘my hooptie’): p.Possessor/p.Possessor. ‘my PA’ or ‘my 3 year old’ as social relation: p.SocialRel/p.Gestalt.
- Genitive event noun subject/actor can be p.Agent/p.Gestalt (‘car’s work’ example p.Theme/p.Gestalt is also attested); event theme should be read in context. Beneficiary genitive (‘children’s clothing’, ‘bus boys’ station’) can be p.Beneficiary/p.Possessor.

Circumstance and paths:
- ‘Throughout the year’ and ‘for over 7 years’ expressing duration: p.Duration/p.Duration. In ‘over a year’, over is p.Approximator/p.Approximator.
- ‘By saying’ when saying is the means of an act: p.Means/p.Means. ‘By the slice’ is p.SetIteration/p.SetIteration.
- Event/place location (‘at Lovely Nails’, ‘on Military Road’, ‘driving on highway’, ‘in bathroom’): p.Locus/p.Locus. ‘At’ before organization as predicate complement can be p.Org/p.Locus.
- Destination at an institution (‘went to the school’): p.Org/p.Goal; ordinary motion destination (‘go to station’, ‘went to a surgeon’, ‘return to it’): p.Goal/p.Goal. Directional movement governs Goal; static location is Locus. ‘To’ infinitival intended action is Purpose.
- ‘from perfect’ and ‘out of the Wok’ marks source: p.Source/p.Source. ‘Back’ in ‘took it back in’ is p.Direction/p.Direction.
- ‘in’ time (‘in today’s tough times’) is p.Time/p.Time. ‘By this point’ is also p.Time/p.Time.

Other recurring distinctions:
- ‘for’ can be p.Beneficiary/p.Beneficiary for whom an action/service is done; p.Purpose/p.Purpose for intended function (‘things for earrings’, ‘get napkins’, ‘made to suit’); p.ComparisonRef/p.Purpose in ‘too much for daycare’ (degree exceeds comparison standard, construed as purpose); p.Possession/p.Theme in ‘pay 40 dollars for a onesie’; duration in ‘for over a year’; Theme in ‘looking for any way’. Inspect construction.
- ‘to’ infinitive with intended action is p.Purpose/p.Purpose; ‘to suit me’ likewise purpose. But experiencer complement of adjective (‘important to them’) is p.Experiencer/p.Goal.
- ‘with’ in a characteristic construction (‘crap with/over my hair’) can be p.Characteristic/p.Characteristic; emotional adjective ‘pleased with’ is Stimulus/Topic; ‘work with cater’ in ‘easy to work with’ can be Agent/Ancillary; social relation ‘worked with Ted’ is SocialRel/Ancillary.
- ‘like’ in an explicit comparison (‘like driving a new car’) is p.ComparisonRef/p.ComparisonRef; in ‘a surgeon like him’ identity resemblance is p.Identity/p.ComparisonRef; in ‘feel like you are…’ manner role with comparison-reference function: p.Manner/p.ComparisonRef.
- ‘on’ with maintenance ‘on my hooptie’ is p.Theme/p.Theme, while ordinary location on a road is Locus.
- ‘at least’ / ‘at best’ are extent: p.Extent/p.Extent. ‘On all levels’ can be p.Extent/p.Extent.
- ‘job of taking care’ can be p.Identity/p.Identity.
- ‘as’ role is construction-sensitive: ‘as a gift/ member’ identity p.Identity/p.Identity; ‘as much as’ extent-cost p.Cost/p.Extent; ‘as long as’ circumstance; ‘as well’ circumstance.
- ‘in service’ after superlative can be abstract p.Circumstance/p.Circumstance; ordinary spatial descriptive ‘in’ remains Locus.

Always distinguish partitive of (QuantityItem/Whole), stimulus/topic of emotional predicates, and possessive uses. Use Locus for where an event or property holds; use Goal when a directional relation is expressed. For for-phrases, distinguish recipient/beneficiary, purpose, possession/cost, duration, comparison standard, and Theme from the governing predicate and construction.
